metadata.title: Literacy, Numeracy and Problem Solving in Technology-Rich Environments (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD framework document describes how PIAAC domains (literacy, numeracy, and problem solving in technology-rich environments) are defined and how tasks are constructed and interpreted; it does not provide an analytic dataset or an estimation procedure. Because no student-level empirical modeling is conducted here, there is no reported use of complex survey weights or replicate-weight variance estimation. For any downstream empirical use of PIAAC microdata, analysts should apply the official PIAAC sampling weights and replicate weights (if provided in the data products) to account for the multistage clustered design and unequal selection probabilities. The document’s focus is on assessment design (task characteristics, cognitive/technology dimensions, and item distributions), not on weighting choices for statistical inference.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a framework for defining and constructing PIAAC assessment domains rather than an empirical analysis of student responses. It therefore does not report any plausible-value generation/combination strategy or any missing-data handling method because no model estimation is performed. Any PV and missing-data procedures would be specified in the separate PIAAC assessment documentation and data products, not in this domain framework.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic sample is defined because this is a framework document summarizing assessment design features for PIAAC (task/domain definitions, dimensions, and item/task characteristics). It states that PIAAC is implemented by 25 countries and that data collection runs from August 2011 to March 2012, but it does not provide a final analytic dataset or inclusion/exclusion rules for an empirical study.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD framework document specifies what PIAAC measures and how the three assessment domains are operationalized for task development and interpretation: literacy, numeracy, and problem solving in technology-rich environments. It explains that PIAAC is a computer-based assessment of adult skills implemented by 25 countries, with data collection scheduled from August 2011 to March 2012 and results planned for end-2013. The document details domain definitions, including task characteristics and factors affecting task difficulty for literacy and numeracy, and cognitive, technology, and task dimensions for PS-TRE. It also provides item/task examples and distributions of items by medium, context, and task aspects, supporting consistent construction across participating countries. Because it is not an empirical study, it does not report model performance metrics, benchmarks, or statistical effects; its contribution is to standardize measurement for later analyses of adult skills and their correlates.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a non-empirical OECD assessment framework describing domain definitions and task design for PIAAC rather than conducting an analysis with an outcome variable. As a result, there is no student-level analytic sample, no weighting or replicate-weight strategy for estimation, no plausible-value or missing-data handling for models, and no machine-learning methods or predictive results to extract. The appropriate interpretation is that the document supports later empirical work by specifying what constructs should be measured and how tasks should be built and interpreted.
